sm: Hosts Patrick Whitlock and Tate Matthews open the show with a quick look at the weekend, including a Kentucky kicker who made six field goals. The main story is the state cross country meet in Memphis, where the Brentwood girls won their sixth or seventh straight AAA title with 48 points, led by a freshman who placed third. Independence finished third, Ravenwood fifth and Summit seventh, so all four county teams placed in the top seven. On the boys side, Independence finished second on a tiebreaker with 97 points, and Summit's Caden Pease placed third. The hosts then cover bowling, including a 276 game from a Page bowler and a Ravenwood boys win.

The hosts begin by noting the bowling results and then turn to the first round of the football playoffs, where seven county teams played and five won. Fairview beat Stratford 28 to 16, with Wyatt Langford making ten tackles and three sacks. Page routed Portland 63 to 7, and Isaac Odie ran for 101 yards and two touchdowns on five carries. Nolensville shut out Hendersonville 31 to 0, with Ryan Newell throwing three touchdown passes. Antioch beat Franklin 28 to 10, which was the first setback of the weekend, and the hosts discussed how competitive they expected that game to be.

The hosts finish reviewing the playoff results. Franklin's season ended with five losses, and they note that Brentwood, Ravenwood and Antioch, three of those opponents, are still playing. Ravenwood beat Cane Ridge 49 to 0, with Brooks Brown going eight of ten for 160 yards and two touchdowns. Clarksville beat Independence 38 to 7, and Brody Bullock had four catches, ten tackles and a blocked field goal in a losing effort. Brentwood beat Rossview 42 to 8, with Gavin Strang throwing for three touchdowns. In the pick'em contest, Tate went five and two and Patrick four and three, leaving Tate at 52 and 28 and Patrick at 53 and 27.

The hosts make their picks for round two. Both take Fairview against Covington, Nolensville to cover against Kirkwood, and Southwind over Brentwood because of Southwind's speed. They split on Page, who are favored by 23 and a half points over Henry County, with Tate expecting a narrow cover from Henry County and Patrick expecting Page to win but not by that much. Both think Ravenwood will beat Whitehaven but not cover a spread of 15 and a half. They then preview possible later matchups, including Fairview hosting the quarterfinals and Nolensville potentially traveling to Munford.

The hosts discuss Ravenwood possibly hosting Antioch in a later round and the chance of Brentwood traveling to Collierville. They complain that a regional writer's statewide predictions included no Williamson County team in the 6A title game. They congratulate Page athletic director Benji Gray, named Athletic Director of the Year, and Page lacrosse coach Dana Fosano, named female coach of the year in region six. Finally, they discuss the new regional alignments, which put all of the county's 6A schools together in a seven team region and leave Fairview in 3A and Centennial in 5A. The hosts say it should make scheduling easier and expect big gate crowds.
